title: Unit 04 - Organizing Your Work for Worksheets A, B, and C - written instructions
body:
For all worksheets, Wkst A, Wkst B, and Wkst C
All work must be shown for solving each equation / problem.  Your work must communicate your process to the reader. Answers only will not receive credit.

Turning in work:
•    Organize your work for each problem, so that it clearly communicates your thought process. 

•    Calculators are not to be used on any problem. (Well, you can use them to CHECK your answers, but don't rely on them to GET the answer, since you won't be able to on an assessment.)

•    All answers must be exact in fractional/radical form. No decimals should be used. Radicals in the denominator, unless the value is related to a Unit Circle angle, do not need to be rationalized.

•    When working with equations, or any other multi-step problem, your work must be written DOWN the page.  Start a new line for each step.

•    You should skip at least one line between the end of one question and the beginning of another. 

•    Each problem should be numbered in the margin, so that the question numbers stand out and can be easily found.  Be sure to follow each worksheets specific instructions for question numbering.

•    You may put two columns on your paper.  Hint: Fold it in half to make it easy to keep in the column.

•    Do NOT start work for a problem on one page (or column) and finish it on the next.

•    Do not box/circle anything.

If you are still not sure how to format your work, watch the demonstration video.

title: Unit 04 - Verifying Trig Identities (VTI) videos - Basic Techniques
body:
Here are some videos that are essential to you learning the material in Unit 4 and succeeding on the assessments that you will be taking.  In-class instruction will focus on any AP-specific instruction that is needed and practicing of AP style questions.  You will watch these videos for the foundation that you need.

This unit used to be Unit 7 (and Unit 6 before that), so do not panic if you see a different unit number.

Basic Techniques Overview

Rules for Verifying Trig Identities:

You will only manipulate the LEFT side of the identity. (If the more complex side is on the right, then FLIP the identity.)

  • Copy both sides of the identity onto your paper
  • the equal sign and the right side of the identity must be copied in every step - if you leave these off, you no longer have an equation!!
  • Then use identities and algebra to work it until you end up with the left side being identical to what was given on the right side of the identity.

You must show all steps of work in a organized manner to clearly communicate to the reader.  Steps must either be obvious as to what algebra or identity substitution was performed OR additional scratch work off to the side needs to be shown / brief explanation given.

If you do not follow directions, you cannot earn credit.

title: Unit 04 - Worksheet A - Solving Trig Equations (STE)
body:
Worksheet A - Solving Trig Equations

Worksheet A - Problem Picker / Cover Sheet Generator
You MUST generate and print a cover sheet to be turned in with your Worksheet A packet.  Work turned in without a cover sheet WILL NOT be graded.

All equations are to be solved on the interval .  In addition, all Level 3 and Level 4 equations should ALSO include the minimum number of general solutions.

Worksheet A has an opportunity for 30 bonus points. However, to qualify for the bonus points, Worksheet A must be turned in on-time (beginning of the class period on your Unit 4 Test Day) and with the Cover Page printed from the Problem Picker/Cover Sheet Generator web page.

How to format your work for Worksheets A, B, and C:  written instructions    demonstration video

There is no answer key for this worksheet, since you will be turning in your work and it will be graded for accuracy.  However, since you are solving equations, you should already know how to check your answers yourself without an answer key to guide you.
